written.myAnswer: Metallic bonds form between metal atoms; positive metal ions are held together by mobile electrons.
A metallic bond is the attraction between positive metal ions and mobile electrons. An ionic bond is the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.
Metal atoms are arranged in rows that can slip past one another when pressure is applied, allowing metals to be shaped into sheets or drawn into wires.
Mobile electrons transfer heat through the metal.

Mobile electrons make metals good conductors of heat and electricity. The strong metallic bonding and close arrangement of atoms help make metals hard and usually give them high melting and boiling points; their rows can slip past one another, making them malleable and ductile. Metals are also usually heavy and lustrous.
Metal atoms are strongly held together and arranged in rows, which makes metals usually hard and heavy.
